summary: 1 Corinthians 1 (31 verses) continues the story of unity. Starting with 'Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and our brother Sosthenes,', it moves through themes of unity, cross wisdom and calls readers toward resurrection.
whyItMatters: This chapter matters because it shows unity lived out in division, immorality, questions. For a first-time reader, it answers: who is God in this moment, what does he ask, and how do people respond.

keyVerses.text: Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and our brother Sosthenes,
(I also baptized the household of Stephanas; besides them, I don’t know whether I baptized any other.)
that, as it is written, “He who boasts, let him boast in the Lord.”

questions.question: What is happening in 1 Corinthians 1?
questions.answer: In 31 verses, this chapter 1 corinthians 1 (31 verses) continues the story of unity. starting with 'paul, called to be an apostle of jesus christ through the will of god, and our brother sosthenes,', it moves through themes of unity, cross wisdom and calls readers toward resurrection. The setting is division, immorality, questions, written to corinthian church, chaotic port city. Look for who speaks, who listens, and what changes by the end.

questions.question: Who wrote 1 Corinthians and why 1 matters in the bigger story?
questions.answer: Traditionally paul, addressed to corinthian church, chaotic port city around ad 53-55. This chapter fits the book's purpose as letter - pastoral correction — its themes of unity, cross wisdom build on what came before.

questions.question: What does 'righteousness' mean in this chapter?
questions.answer: Being in right standing, doing what is right. In this chapter, it appears in context of unity. For a first-time reader: think of it as being in right standing, doing what is right, not just religious jargon.

questions.question: What does this chapter teach about God or people?
questions.answer: Through unity and cross wisdom, it shows God's character (faithful, just, merciful) and human tendency (need, failure, hope). Notice how verses move from problem to provision.

questions.question: Verse 10 is long — what is it saying in plain English?
questions.answer: The verse says: 'Now I beg you, brothers, through the name of our Lord, Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be perfected together...' In plain terms: it is making a key point about unity. Break it into two halves — what is described, and what is promised or commanded.

questions.question: How could this chapter apply today without forcing modern ideas onto it?
questions.answer: Ask: what was original audience supposed to do with this? Then ask: what similar situation exists today? For example, if chapter warns about idols, today that might be money or status; if it celebrates deliverance, where do people need deliverance today?
